text:
anna-sales: AcmeHealth POC blocked for 11am demo, reports 403 with 'invalid_org_claim' from our API. Can sales+eng take a quick look? acme-ops is on the thread.
acme-ops: Repro steps: hitting our app which proxies to Redwood. Example curl from our host: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_test_ABC' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"redwood-1","input":"ping"}'``` Payload returns `{"error":"invalid_org_claim","detail":"request missing org header binding"}` After a few quick retries we then saw `429 Too Many Requests`.
tom-se: thanks. Two likely failure modes: 1) token is scoped to a project but you're calling an org-level route, or 2) an intermediate proxy is stripping the required org header. Can you paste the outbound request headers as your proxy sends them (redact keys)?
acme-ops: proxy logs show we set `Authorization`, `User-Agent: acme/proxy-1.3`, and `X-Project-ID: proj-77`. No `X-ORG-ID`. Our proxy does some header normalization; might be dropping custom headers.
lucy-eng: that explains it. If the token is project-bound, the service expects either a project-scoped endpoint (https://api.redwood.ai/v1/projects/proj-77/generate) or the request must include the org binding header (X-ORG-ID). Without the header you'll get invalid_org_claim. Quick fix: change the target URL to the project-scoped route in your proxy config.
edith-support: additional note: the client side retrier retried 8x at fixed intervals which tripped the global rate limiter after the initial 403s. Recommend enabling exponential backoff (client lib v2.1.3+) and honoring Retry-After. Also set REDWOOD_SDK_DEBUG=1 to capture the response headers for trace.
acme-ops: is there any non-config change we can do for the demo? We can't rotate keys right now.
lucy-eng: temporary workaround without rotating keys: 1) Point proxy to `https://api.redwood.ai/v1/projects/proj-77/generate`. 2) If you must use the org route, inject `X-ORG-ID: org-acme` into proxied requests (but only if your proxy can be trusted to set that header safely). 3) Add short jitter/backoff to avoid 429s.
julia-ps: sales note: for short demos we can issue a time-limited org-scoped key (24h) if they want to keep the original endpoint. That avoids touching their proxy. I'd need to run this by sales-ops. Pricing: project keys inherit trial quotas; if they expect bursty demo traffic we can enable a small burst window (one-off) — I'll start the internal request.
infra-bot: [infra] observed pattern: 7x 403 then 429 from ip 34.82.91.4 within 3 minutes. Marked as "transient demo storm" and throttled.
edith-support: opening SUP-12788, attaching proxy logs and our recommended steps. Marked P1 for the demo window.
acme-ops: switched proxy target to project-scoped route and enabled jitter/backoff in our client. Tests now return 200 and valid generation payload. Thanks!
anna-sales: great, can someone drop a 1-paragraph blurb about token binding behavior and the temporary org-key option for Acme's security questionnaire? acme wants that in 30 mins.
julia-ps: I'll draft the blurb and the quick checklist (what to change in proxy, which SDK version to use, and demo traffic suggestions). Posting in 20.
an-na: thanks team, looping back to client after julia posts the blurb. :thumbsup:
